text:
Ava - Growth: Hey runtime team — we need a focused rerun for the launch claim checks. Goal: validate coldstart heatmap + quantized variant numbers so marketing can lock copy. Need: 95th/99th latencies, cold vs warmed percentiles, token-cost per request, and a short delta vs fp16. Please run: redwood-13b-v2-quantized and a fallback redwood-13b-v2-fp16. Target region: us-west1. Sample size: ~5k requests across seeds + long-context tail. Also include a small reproducible payload pack we can link to in the blog.

Jun (Runtime): Got it — couple clarifying Qs before we schedule:
- exact model id (is that the rl13b-v2-quant? we have a couple builds)
- desired load profile (QPS, burst, and duration)
- do you want embedding calls included in the sweep or just generation?
- are there any hard SLA targets we should try to meet or just capture raw numbers?

Ava - Growth: Use model id redwood-13b-v2-quantized (the one listed in the deck). Profile: 50 QPS sustained for 10m, with 1m coldstart probes every 2m to capture heatmap. Include embedding calls for the demo path (separate tag). No hard SLA — capture raw numbers and percentiles; call out 95th and 99th. Marketing will want a one-paragraph headline and a one-slide table with delta vs fp16.

Rohan (Eng Runtime): We can run that. Quick notes:
- quantized runs will sometimes hit a small quality delta — do you have an eval prompt set for comparing output degradation? recommend adding an "eval-suite-launch-2026" set so we can measure BLEU/EM/embedding-sim.
- warmup: default 30s per instance, but for 50 QPS sustained we'll do a 90s ramp to mirror production.
- we'll tag results with job id and attach raw traces. Need the sample payload JSON to be exact. Do you want us to pin a rolling cache policy for the run?

Ava - Growth: Yes please add eval-suite-launch-2026. Pin cache policy off for the quantized run (we want worst-case). For fp16 fallback run, enable normal prefix cache. Here's a tiny example payload set to include (we'll upload the full pack to the drive and reference it in the blog):

```
[
  {"id": "s1", "prompt": "Summarize product launch in one sentence.", "max_tokens": 60},
  {"id": "s2", "prompt": "List 5 benefits of Redwood's dedicated inference for enterprise.", "max_tokens": 120},
  {"id": "s3-long", "prompt": "<long-context: 6k tokens> Explain how caching affects coldstart and per-token costs.", "max_tokens": 256},
  {"id": "s4-short", "prompt": "What's the latency?", "max_tokens": 16}
]
```

Also include a 10% slice of long-tail conversational prompts (we'll upload full file marketing-seed-v3.json to the shared drive). Please tag runs: marketing-launch-quant and marketing-launch-fp16.

bench-bot: Job scheduled: job_id=mk-launch-2026-88, queue ETA ~2h. Artifacts will be at: https://internal-artifacts/redwood/mk-launch-2026-88. Notifying #eng-runtime. :robot_face:

Jun (Runtime): Noted — a couple constraints to flag here:
- quantized variant currently only available on our p4d pools in us-west1; if demand exceeds reserved capacity we may auto-fallback to fp16 earlier than expected. We'll surface capacity warnings during the run.
- for eval: we'll compute embedding-sim and token-level divergence and attach a short markdown summary. Expect the initial artifact bundle ~3h after job completion.

Marta (Marketing Ops): Thx team — quick ask for timeline: can we get preliminary numbers and a 1-sentence headline by EOD tomorrow if run starts within 2h? If not, what's a realistic ETA so we can adjust the launch comms plan?

Rohan (Eng Runtime): If the run starts within the hour we can deliver preliminary percentiles + headline draft in ~18 hours (includes eval pass). Full artifacts and traces ~36 hours. If that works say :thumbsup: and we'll lock the schedule.

Ava - Growth: :thumbsup: Lock it. Please make the headline include an explicit cost delta per 1k tokens vs fp16 if feasible. And call out any quality regression >2% on eval-suite as a blocker for the quantized claim. Thanks all — will watch the artifacts link and pull the slide once results land.
